description: Iteratively apply repulsive forces and uniform radius inflation to jointly optimise centres and radii.

guidance.idea: Start from a random or low‑discrepancy placement, then repeatedly (1) compute repulsive forces between circles and from walls, (2) move centres a small step along the forces, (3) uniformly increase radii until an overlap is detected, (4) project back into the feasible region.
guidance.transfer_rule: N/A (template for any packing / layout problem where forces can be defined).
actions: Initialize centres `c_i` randomly in the unit square.
• Compute pairwise vectors `d_ij = c_i - c_j` and distances `||d_ij||`.
• For each pair, add a repulsive force proportional to `max(0, r_i+r_j - ||d_ij||)`.
• Add wall‑repulsion forces for circles near the boundaries.
• Update centres with a small step size `η`.
• Increase all radii by a small increment `Δr` and clip to keep circles inside the square.
• If any overlap appears, roll back the last radius increment.
cautions: Step sizes η and Δr must be tuned; too large leads to instability.
Terminate after a fixed number of iterations or when total radius change < ε.
